c.tagline: Borneo's cat city — riverfront heritage and a gateway to orangutans and rainforest.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but Grab is far cheaper and more reliable; agree a fare first if taking a non-metered taxi.

emergency.note: 999 reaches police, ambulance and fire nationwide; 112 also works from mobile phones.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Padungan: Great Cat of Kuching statue, Padungan

hood_desc: The riverside promenade and colonial old town — Main Bazaar antiques, the Brooke-era courthouse, Chinese temples and the famous Cat Statue, with the Astana and Fort Margherita across the water; the sightseeing heart.
Kuching's Chinatown and café district along Jalan Padungan, lined with heritage shophouses, coffee shops, cocktail bars and the city's main nightlife; lively after dark.
A narrow heritage lane of Chinese temples, kopitiams, craft workshops and boutique guesthouses tucked behind the Main Bazaar; atmospheric, arty and walkable.
A local, riverside district famous for its big weekend market of jungle produce and Dayak crafts; down-to-earth and authentic away from the tourist core.
A modern residential and commercial zone around The Spring mall and Swinburne University, with malls and chain hotels; quieter and handy for shopping and day-trip departures.

water.note: Tap water is treated and better than most of Malaysia, but most people still boil or drink bottled.

transit.pay: Buses are paid in cash to the driver (about RM1-4); the Kuching hydrogen SmartBus loops the city centre. Small wooden sampan (tambang) river taxis cross the Sarawak River for around RM1.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to 7pm; sampan river taxis run through the evening. After dark most travel is by Grab.
transit.note: Kuching has no rail transit. Getting around is by Grab, buses and the traditional sampan river taxis that ferry people across the Sarawak River between the Waterfront and the Astana/Fort Margherita side.

ferry: Pending Wharf (Express Bahagia boat to Sibu)

transit.m: Airport coupon taxi to city centre

tip.r: Tipping is not expected; a service charge is often already added at hotels and upscale restaurants.
